title: He called it urgency.
paragraphs:
He called it urgency.
God called it disobedience.
Because this is where it gets uncomfortable.

You can look spiritual…
and still be out of alignment with God.

Saul wasn’t chasing idols.
He wasn’t bowing to false gods.
He was standing beside an altar.

What if the thing you’re doing “for God”…
is actually a cover for not trusting Him?
What if your urgency is just fear in disguise?

What if your “I had no choice”
is really
“I didn’t want to wait”?
Because Saul’s story is not ancient history.

The army was slipping away.
Fear was spreading like wildfire.
The enemy was gathering.
But waiting started to feel like losing.
Grabbed the priestly role that wasn’t his.
“You have done foolishly. You have not kept the command of the LORD your God… For then the LORD would have established your kingdom over Israel forever. But now your kingdom shall not continue…”

He didn’t commit murder.
He didn’t deny God publicly.
He simply refused to obey fully.

And religious activity
can still be rebellion
when the heart refuses surrender.

You prayed…
but you also manipulated.

You said “God, I trust You”…
but still forced the outcome.

You posted Scripture…
but hid compromise in private.

You rushed decisions,
crossed lines,
justified shortcuts—

When pressure rises,
obedience feels negotiable.

When silence stretches,
control feels necessary.

When fear gets loud,
faith gets quiet.
“I know better than God in this moment.”
But Scripture cuts through that illusion.
“Trust in the LORD with all your heart, and do not lean on your own understanding. In all your ways acknowledge Him, and He will make straight your paths.”

Even the urgent ones.
Especially the urgent ones.
Now feel the weight of this:

Saul lost a kingdom
not because he was weak—
but because he refused to trust God under pressure.
Because this is where grace breaks in.

Where Saul grabbed control—
Jesus surrendered control.

Where Saul disobeyed under pressure—
Jesus obeyed under pressure so intense
He sweat blood in Luke 22:42:
“Father, if You are willing, remove this cup from Me. Nevertheless, not My will, but Yours, be done.”
Jesus had every reason to avoid the cross.

Your impulsive decisions
are not the end of your story.

Your “unlawful sacrifices”
do not have the last word.
“But God shows His love for us in that while we were still sinners, Christ died for us.”
While you were still choosing control.

You sinned.
You rushed.
You disobeyed.

But Jesus obeyed in your place,
died for your sin,
and rose again to give you new life.

The delay you hate
may be the protection you don’t see.

The waiting you resist
may be forming the faith you need.
You don’t need to fix everything.
Jesus is not pushing you away.
“The sacrifices of God are a broken spirit; a broken and contrite heart, O God, You will not despise.”
God is not looking for perfect performance.
He is looking for surrendered hearts.
If this stirred something in you…
